transcription.notes: One top-level task (Main Telescope) with five printed sub-tasks 1.–5., transcribed as parts. Problems page 2 is the answer sheet with Chart 1 (cropped as p1-fig1); problems page 3 carries only the letterhead and is blank. The solutions document restates the task in a different wording and with different points (20, 10, 25, 20, 25 Point instead of 23, 10, 21, 21, 25 points); it is transcribed as printed at the start of the solution, and the part points follow the problems document. The solutions document prints the declination as -34° 49” (double prime) while the problems document prints -34° 49’; both kept verbatim. Solutions page 2 repeats the blank Chart 1 (answer sheet), cropped as p1-sol-fig1; the solution chart with cardinal directions and scoring circles is p1-sol-fig2. The FOV formula is kept as printed (with the letter x as multiplication sign). The solutions page 2 heading is printed „Anwer Sheet“ and kept verbatim. The graphic at the top of every page is the IOAA 2015 letterhead (logos), decoration, not a figure.

parts.statement:
Point your telescope to NGC 6475 (M7)

RA (J2000): 17h 53m 54s

Dec (J2000): -34$^{\circ}$ 49’

Show the object to your telescope assistant. If you fail to find the object in the first 10 minutes, ask the assistant to help, but you will lose the mark. (23 points)
Write down the cardinal directions (North, South, East and West) on Chart 1 in the answer sheet. (10 points)
Three stars of M7 are missing from the Chart 1. Mark the position of the missing stars with crosses (x). (21 points)

The apparent magnitudes of comparison stars A, B and C are 7.6, 7.2, and 5.6 respectively. Estimate and write down the apparent magnitudes of the missing stars beside respective cross marks. (21 points)
Estimate the FOV of the instrument, using the given stopwatch. Show your calculation in the answer sheet. (25 points)

solution.statement:
**Observational Problem**

**Main Telescope**

1. Point your telescope to NGC 6475

   RA (J2000): 17h 53m 54s

   Dec (J2000): -34$^{\circ}$ 49”

   Validate your object to your telescope assistant. (20 Point)

2. Write down the cardinal direction (North, South, East and West) on Chart 1 in the answer sheet. (10 Point)

3. Find 3 missing stars on Chart 1 based on the object you have observed. Mark the position of the missing stars with crosses (X). (25 Point)

4. Given that the magnitude of star A, B and C are 7.6, 7.2, and 5.6 respectively. Estimate and write down the magnitude of the missing stars beside each mark you have given. (20 Point)

5. Estimate the FOV of the eyepiece in this observation, stopwatch provided. Show your calculation in the answer sheet. (25 Point)

Anwer Sheet

Chart 1

Solution,

1. Checklist: (Telescope Assistant)

- Object Accuracy (Right Object = Full Score).

Answer

No 2 (Cardinal Point) — Each Correct Cardinal Point (Quarter Score)

No 3 (three missing stars) — Region 1 (Full Score), 2 (Half Score), 3 (Quarter Score)

Note: The region are marked with the circles (region will be chosen during the IBM)

4. Missing Stars:

| | |
|---|---|
| 1. | 7.4 |
| 2. | 6.4 |
| 3. | 7.0 |

Score Range:

$\pm 0.2$ = Full Score

$\pm 0.5$ = Half Score

$\pm 0.8$ = Quarter Score

5. Using the 15mm (eyepiece), the field of view of the instrument is: 0.75$^{\circ}$

- Using stopwatch to measure the time for a star to travel from the center of the FOV to the edge of the FOV. (Half Score)
- Using stopwatch to measure the time for a star to travel from the edge of the FOV to the other edge of the FOV (Quarter Score)
- Calculating the FOV,

$$FOV(\mathrm{deg}) = \frac{Travel\ time(\mathrm{sec})}{23h\ 56m} x cos(\delta) x 360 deg$$

(Half Score)
